messages.subject: internal discussion of proposals
messages.body_plain:
Mentors,

We've got one more week to finalize our slot requests to Google.

We need you, as mentors, to do a couple of things.

If you received only one proposal for your project idea, please add a
comment in the comments section describing your feelings about the
proposal, including any red flags or misgivings or incomplete bits.  It
would be ideal if you also describe the contact you've had so far with
the student. Comments made in the comment slot on the 'Proposal View'
page are only visible to other R mentors, not to the students.

Additionally, you *must* click the button "Want to Mentor" on your
preferred proposal.  We cannot assign slots without mentors, and it
doesn't look like we as admins can assign extra mentors to slots who
have not already indicated their willingness to mentor.  So we need at
least on mentor marking 'want to mentor' before next Friday, and we will
need two or more before final slot assignment.

For mentors who received two or more proposals, you should have already
received my message from last weekend requesting additional information
to help us compare your multiple proposals.  It would be idea if those
receiving multiple proposals could add their comments in the Proposal
View comment section as well.

Please feel free to contact me or the other administrators with any
questions.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

proposals as more reach a ready to be assigned status for us.

Brian

Many proposals do not have mentors selecting 'Want to Mentor' or

proposal.  If you received only one student application, we still need

said in many emails over the past few weeks.

you as well.  Additionally, you should already have been in touch with

the applications received.

Please help us out by making sure your commentary is complete and on the
Google site.

Slot requests are due to Google later today.

Incomplete information or communication will be interpreted as a lack of
commitment.

Regards,

Brian

messages.subject: R receives 25 slots and next steps
messages.subject_clean: R receives 25 slots and next steps
messages.body_plain:
R has been granted (up to) 25 slots for this year's Google Summer of
Code.

This shows a great deal of trust placed in the R community by Google,
and should once again make R one of the top organizations receiving
slots for Google Summer of Code.

Our next step is to assign those slots.

Students, we are prohibited by Google from discussing slot assignments
with you.  Until the Google announcements happen, you need to sit tight,
and let the process work.  Thank you for all your hard work so far, and
good luck.

Mentors, you will start to see projects being marked as 'Accepted' in
the GSoC management system.  Some of you have received or will receive
emails from me or one of the other org. admins requesting more
information.  As we have said preciously, if you have not selected 'Want
to Mentor' and commented on your project applications, you will not get
a slot.  If you have not communicated with me, Toby, Virgilio, and John
when asked, you will not get a slot.  If you feel we are ignoring or not
attending to an application you want to mentor, please contact us via
email immediately. We need your cooperation in a timely manner over the
next several days.

We have a lot of work to do in the next few days, and no flexibility on
timing.  Google's deadlines are firm, and there are no exceptions.

If anyone has any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me and
the other R org. admins.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: Fwd: Community Bonding Principles
messages.body_plain:
>From Google, I thought it was relevant to the entire R GSOC community - Brian
---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: "Google Summer of Code" <summerofco...@google.com>
Date: Apr 28, 2016 7:32 PM
Subject: Community Bonding Principles
To: <bgpbra...@gmail.com>
Cc:

Hi Brian G. Peterson,

By now, you should have already welcomed your student(s) to GSoC 2016.

If you have not been in contact with your student, reach out to them as soon as possible to welcome them into your community.

Community Bonding Period
As part of the student’s acceptance into GSoC they are expected to actively participate in the Community Bonding period (April 22 - May 22). The Community Bonding period is intended to get students ready to start contributing to your organization full time in May.

Unfortunately, some students think their acceptance into GSoC guarantees them the initial $500 payment. That is not the case. A student does not receive $500 just for writing a good proposal. They must be active in the Community Bonding period to earn that $500.

Community Bonding activities may involve:
Becoming familiar with the community practices and processes. (This often involves a mix of observation and participation.)
Participating on Mailing Lists / IRC / etc. (Not just lurking.)
Setting up their development environment.
Small (or large) patches/bug fixes. (These do not need to be directly related to their GSoC project.)
Participating in code reviews for others. (Even someone who isn't familiar with the project can contribute by pointing out potential inefficiencies, bad error handling, etc.)
Working with their mentor and other org members on refining their project plan. This might include finalizing deadlines and milestones, adding more detail, figuring out potential issues, etc.
If the student is already familiar with the organization, they could be helping others get involved in the community.
Reading (and updating!) documentation they will need to understand to complete their project.
Reporting or replicating bugs.

Active means active. Students have committed to the program schedule, and we would like you to hold them to it. There is no simple standard, as every org is different, every student has different time constraints, and there are many different ways to interact. Some students may require coaxing and encouragement in order to get them to actively participate.

If you do not see regular public interaction from the student, you should strongly encourage it. Public is important -- it is a key principle of open source -- work happens where everyone can see it. Similarly, all work done by the students should be shared in a publicly available repository.

By May 16th if the student has not been active in Community Bonding please notify Google at gsoc-s...@google.com to let us know. After a brief investigation, we may remove the student from the program. They will not receive any payments.

Do not feel bad about "failing" a student.
The past eleven years of GSoC have demonstrated that students who don't interact early and often are more likely to fail later. Often they just disappear. We don't want you to waste your time on students who don't care about the project/organization and can’t even attempt to show interest these first few weeks of the program. Small contributions early on are often a very positive signal.

Organizations will not be penalized for failing students who are not fulfilling their responsibilities during the Community Bonding period. We expect there to be students who fail this Community Bonding period, just like we expect there to be some students who fail the midterm and others that fail the final. This is completely normal.

If you have questions as to whether a student has met the guidelines, don't hesitate to ask. Email gsoc-s...@google.com with a summary of the student's activities during the Community Bonding period, and we will review it.

Best,
Stephanie, Cat, Mary, Robert, Helen and Josh

This email was sent to bgpbra...@gmail.com <http://bgp...@gmail.com>.

You are receiving this email because of your participation in Google Summer of Code 2016.
https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com

To leave the program and stop receiving all emails, you can go to your profile <https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/dashboard/profile/> and request deletion of your program profile.

For any questions, please contact gsoc-s...@google.com. Replies to this message go to an unmonitored mailbox.

© 2016 Google Inc., 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA

messages.body_plain:
Hi, all

I am a student doing the project "Implementation of Recurrent Models and Examples in R for MXNet" this year.

MXNet is a lightweight and flexible deep learning framework which provides a portable backend that can be called from R side.

I aim to implement some important deep learning models in R for the MXNet package. The main component of the work in this year is the implementation of the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) models and examples. In addition, I will also implement some useful examples in R, such as different image classification models and fully convolutional networks for image segmentation. At the same time, I will write sufficient tests and relevant documentations.

The link of the proposal in google doc is
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qSrGqBTXTw6jbuw1X1VGmmmmlLQwWnMUegNx0GSzZvY/edit?usp=sharing

I will prepare for contributing to the organization and try to start coding during the Community Bonding period.

I appreciate it if anyone give me some suggestions or help and I am willing to help others at any time if needed.

Best wishes,
Yuqi Li

We don't want you to waste your time on students who don't care about the project/organization and can’t even attempt to show interest these first few weeks of the program. Small contributions early on are often a very positive signal.
>
> Organizations will not be penalized for failing students who are not fulfilling their responsibilities during the Community Bonding period. We expect there to be students who fail this Community Bonding period, just like we expect there to be some students who fail the midterm and others that fail the final. This is completely normal.
>
> If you have questions as to whether a student has met the guidelines, don't hesitate to ask. Email gsoc-s...@google.com with a summary of the student's activities during the Community Bonding period, and we will review it.
>
> Best,

messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone, nice meeting you!

I'm Eric, a student this year with the project "plot.xts for Performance and Risk".
Here is the the link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B6hlTfwl1uGWNUhMaGZuQTFGeVk/view?usp=sharing.

xts::plot.xts is a strong engine for statistical and financial charting. However quantmod, PerformanceAnalytics, PortfolioAnalytics, quantstrat and blotter packages are using basic R graphical functions. My work is to enhance the flexibility, efficiency and visualization ability by substituing plot.xts for basic graphical functions in those packages and extend the existing examples using the modified functions. Also I will add some dynamic features to the new functions using dygraphs, ggviz or highcharter, finally writing tests and documentations and create vignettes. As PerformanceAnalytics and PortfolioAnalytics packages are using svn on r-forge, I've joined the project and started working on it. For sure I will create a repo on Github as well.

Your comments are most welcome! Many thanks in advance.

Regards,
Eric
